items.summary_orig: Originally published on Shipfolio . What llms.txt is llms.txt is a proposed convention (llmstxt.org) for a plain-text Markdown file at the root of your domain that tells AI assistants what your site is, what matters on it and where to start reading. Where robots.txt tells crawlers where not to go, llms.txt tells a model where to begin.

items.title: 可读的 Linux 目录为何仍可能拒绝进入
items.title_orig: The Doorway Bit: Why a Readable Linux Directory Can Still Refuse Entry
items.summary: 目录的读权限只负责列出名称，执行权限才允许把名称当作路径使用，含义与普通文件不同。
items.summary_orig: A directory displays r-- in its permissions. It is readable, so opening files inside it should work—right? Linux says otherwise. For directories, the familiar permission letters describe different operations than they do for ordinary files. Read permission reveals the directory’s list of names. Execute permission allows those names to be used as paths.

items.title_orig: ALMA Reveals a Dying Star's Final Breath, Encoded In a Giant Ring of Gas
items.summary: 大约6500年前，一颗垂死的恒星发出了最后的“热脉冲”。这最后的喘息形成了 ALMA 探测到的巨大气体环。然后，就在700年前，这颗恒星形成了一个沙漏星云。理论上已经预测到这一点，但这是第一个支持这一点的直接证据。
items.summary_orig: About 6,500 years ago, a dying star emitted its final thermal pulse. That dying breath created a giant ring of gas detected by ALMA. Then only 700 years ago, the star formed an hourglass nebula. Theory predicted this, but this is the first direct evidence supporting it.

items.title: 如何在 Docker 中把 Postgres 升级到 19，以及我遇到的 4 个错误

items.summary: 只改镜像标签无法升级，需导出旧集群恢复到 19，或在同一容器内用两个版本的二进制运行 pg_upgrade。
items.summary_orig: Short answer: you can't upgrade Postgres in Docker by changing the image tag. postgres:19 refuses to start on a data directory from 17 or 18. You either dump the old cluster and restore it into a fresh 19 one (simple, needs downtime about as long as the restore), or you run pg_upgrade with both versions' binaries in one container (fast, a few more traps).

Trained the model from scratch on that, using flow matching in a pretrained autoencoder's latent space.

items.summary_orig: The Simons Observatory is online and surveying the Cosmic Microwave Background (CMB) in greater detail than ever before.
